tasks.title: Site: design tokens, a professional type scale, and DESIGN.md
tasks.body:
Brief: get the basic site right first, and make it read as a professional personal site (docs/briefs/swarm-dogfood-portfolio.md, PRODUCT.md).

Replace the seed styles in `scripts/build.mjs` with CSS custom properties for a type scale, spacing steps and colours (light and dark), and restyle the generated page with them.

Acceptance:
- All sizes, spaces and colours in the CSS come from tokens.
- Looks deliberate at 375 px and 1280 px, light and dark (screenshots in the PR).
- Run `/impeccable document` to record the resulting system in `DESIGN.md`, then `/impeccable critique` on the built page and fix every P0/P1.
- `npm run build && npm run check:site` passes; HTML+CSS stays under budget.

tasks.title: Site: contrast and heading-order rules in check:site
tasks.body:
Brief success: checks stay green and mean something.

Extend `scripts/checks/site.mjs` so it fails when heading levels skip (h1 to h3) and when text/background and accent/background colour pairs in the built CSS fall below WCAG AA (4.5:1) in either colour scheme.

Acceptance:
- Still dependency-free.
- A deliberately broken copy of the page shows each new rule failing; paste the output in the PR.
- The current site passes, or the PR fixes it.

tasks.title: Generator: project cards from the Projects section
tasks.body:
Brief: one description in, a complete portfolio out.

Bullets under `## Projects` in the form `**Name**: one-liner` (optionally with a link) render as project cards (`<article>` with heading, text and link) instead of a plain list.

Acceptance:
- `parse()` exposes projects as structured items; other sections are unchanged.
- Tests cover a project with and without a link.
- `npm test` and `npm run build && npm run check:site` pass.

tasks.title: Site: responsive project card layout
tasks.body:
Brief: the basic site must look professional on a phone and a desktop.

Lay out project cards (from the generator project-cards task; the plain list until that lands) as one column on phones and a grid on wide screens, with no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

Acceptance:
- Uses the design tokens; screenshots at 320, 768 and 1280 px in the PR.
- `/impeccable critique` on the page, every P0/P1 fixed.
- `npm run check:site` passes.

tasks.title: Generator: optional front matter for role, location and links
tasks.body:
Brief: the description is the single source of the person's content.

Support an optional `---` front-matter block at the top of `description.md` with `role`, `location` and `links` (label: url). Absent keys change nothing.

Acceptance:
- Dependency-free parsing; an unknown key is a warning, not a crash.
- Role and location appear in the header; links appear in the header or contact section.
- Tests for: no front matter, partial front matter, unknown key.

tasks.title: Generator: line-numbered errors for unreadable descriptions
tasks.body:
When the description cannot render well (no name heading, empty section, duplicate section titles), the build exits non-zero with `description.md:<line>: <what to fix>`.

Acceptance:
- Each case has a test asserting the message and the line number.
- The sample description builds with no warnings.

tasks.title: Server: local Node server that serves the built site
tasks.body:
Brief: counter and messages need a small local server with SQLite, for testing only. This task lays the base; no counter or messages yet.

Add `server/server.mjs` (no dependencies) exporting `startServer({ port, dbPath, distDir })`. It serves `dist/` and opens a SQLite database with `node:sqlite` at `dbPath` (default a gitignored `data/guest.db`). Add `npm start` (build, then serve on localhost).

Acceptance:
- `server/server.test.mjs` starts the server on port 0 with a temp database, fetches `/` and `/styles.css`, and shuts down cleanly.
- The database path is gitignored; nothing is deployed.
- `npm test` passes.

tasks.title: Server: guest counter for home-page views
tasks.body:
Brief: a guest counter (assumption: it counts home-page views, not unique visitors). Depends on the local server task; leave this unclaimed until that merges.

Each request for `/` increments a count stored in SQLite; `GET /api/visits` returns `{ "visits": n }`.

Acceptance:
- End-to-end test: three requests to `/` give `visits: 3` on a fresh temp database.
- The count survives a server restart on the same database.
- `npm test` passes.

tasks.title: Site: show the visit count on the page
tasks.body:
Brief: visitors see the guest counter. Depends on the guest counter task.

Show the current visit count in the footer when the site is served by the local server. The static `dist/` still opens without the server (the count is simply absent).

Acceptance:
- End-to-end test: the served home page contains the count.
- `npm run check:site` passes; `/impeccable critique` on the footer, every P0/P1 fixed.

tasks.title: Server: guest messages API with SQLite
tasks.body:
Brief: guests leave messages without logging in; no moderation, only length limits and escaping (assumption: optional name, newest first). Depends on the local server task.

`POST /api/messages` accepts `{ name?, text }` (form or JSON); `GET /api/messages` returns the latest 50, newest first.

Acceptance:
- Rejects empty text and text over 500 characters, and names over 60, with a 400 and a clear message.
- Stored as plain text; HTML is escaped wherever it is rendered.
- End-to-end tests for post, list order, and each rejection.
- `npm test` passes.

tasks.title: Site: guestbook form and message list
tasks.body:
Brief: visitors leave a message and see what others left. Depends on the guest messages API task.

Add a guestbook section with a form (optional name, message) and the latest messages, newest first. It works as a plain form post without JavaScript.

Acceptance:
- End-to-end test: posting through the form shows the message on the next page load, escaped.
- `/impeccable critique` on the section, every P0/P1 fixed; `npm run check:site` passes.

tasks.title: UI: dashboard home that says what this swarm builds
tasks.body:
Brief: the dashboard is separate from the product. It explains the swarm, never embeds or rebuilds the portfolio.

Make `swarm-ui` `/` state in one or two lines what this swarm is building (from swarm.config.ts) and link to targets, results and board.

Acceptance:
- Works when swarm memory is unreachable.
- `/impeccable critique` on the page, every P0/P1 fixed.
- `npm --prefix swarm-ui run build` passes.

tasks.title: UI: give the dashboard its own consistent theme
tasks.body:
Set `theme.cssVars` in `swarm-ui/app/swarm/swarm.config.ts` so the dashboard has one consistent accent, background and text palette in light and dark. It stays visually separate from the product.

Acceptance:
- Only `swarm.config.ts` (and at most `swarm.css` variables) change.
- Screenshots in light and dark; `/impeccable critique`, every P0/P1 fixed; `npm --prefix swarm-ui run build` passes.
